articles.title: Is It Really Rude to Decorate Your House Early for Halloween?
articles.content:
我的朋友艾琳对万圣节如此痴迷，以至于她的地下室有两个房间用来存放万圣节装饰品。当大多数人将客房留给人类客人时，她的客房里却住着六个12英尺高的骷髅巨人。此外，里面还塞满了50多个人体大小的骷髅、狗和猫的骷髅、闪烁的灯光、噪音机器，甚至还有一个用骷髅鹿重新创作的圣诞雪橇壁画。

所以，当她在六月就开始筹划10月31日的庆祝活动时，我只能点头并递给她一些玉米糖。然而，我却站在了另一个极端：我是个万圣节的坏脾气。除非你把我七年前安装在车库附近的橙色闪烁灯泡算作装饰，否则我根本不装饰。但这不仅仅是懒惰的问题。说实话，我真的不喜欢万圣节。孩子们的装扮游戏？太棒了，让我们天天这样。但其他一切，我都能省略。我最讨厌的是令人毛骨悚然的恐怖院子装饰，因为我是个大胆小心的懦夫。有一段环形摄像头视频在我的邻居中流传，我被一个突然弹出来的手吓得尖叫着跑开了。

然而，艾琳和我是最亲密的朋友！我认为我们在假日氛围上互相平衡。尽管如此，我们在一个重大问题上意见分歧：什么时候可以放出万圣节装饰？早点装饰房子真的算是无礼吗？到底有多早算太早？答案可能介于她的“独立日之后”和我的“永不”之间。因此，为了本文的目的，我把“早”定义为10月1日之前。

现在，戴上你的巫婆帽，让我们讨论一下。

**你的房子，你的规矩。**这是为任何节日装饰房子的最佳理由。你花了不少钱买那块草地，所以应该可以按照自己的喜好装饰（在公共礼仪的范围内）。看起来很多人都在这样做。根据2024年YouGov的一项调查，52%的人表示在10月之前就看到了万圣节装饰品——13%的人表示在劳动节前就看到了。是的，有些人已经为开学季准备了骷髅装饰。（有些人甚至全年都保留骷髅装饰！）

这确实有道理：如果你喜欢万圣节，越早布置装饰，就有越多时间享受乐趣。这也激发了邻里的友谊，为人们夜间遛狗时提供娱乐。它甚至可能激励他们也变得更加节日化。在这个住宅业主协会规定每一种颜色和灌木摆放的世界里，这是你变得疯狂的时刻。

提前装饰也可以帮助你应对天气，如果你住在气候非常“剧烈”的地方。我们住在明尼苏达州时，居民在九月就挂起了圣诞灯——不是因为他们非常愉快，而是因为没人想在十二月的大雪和零下10度时爬上屋顶。万圣节装饰也在第一场大雪之前布置好，是的，这意味着有时你会同时看到橙色南瓜灯和红绿色屋顶灯。这总比冻伤好！

所以，九月的某个星期二，草地上爬出一个巨大的骷髅躯干，是不是有点过分？大概吧。但关于怀旧带来的那种特定的欢乐和期待，有一些值得一提的东西，而没有任何东西能像装饰品一样触发这种感觉。谁没有过一个美好的秋季记忆，和朋友们一起出去，穿着超级英雄的衣服，在灯光闪烁的街区里奔跑，吃着糖果？看？你已经笑了。

“你的房子，你的规矩”是正确的，但你的房子（可能）位于一个社区中，这些人可以对他们的环境发表意见——包括何时会有不死者出现。人们确实对此有感受：另一项2024年YouGov调查发现，39%的人表示10月1日到10月15日是最早可以放万圣节装饰的时间，24%的人表示在劳动节后就可以。只有4%的人表示更早也没问题。

前一部分提到的万圣节装饰“在公共礼仪的范围内”这句话实际上做了很多工作，在我看来，这正是争议的焦点。有趣的骷髅和可笑的墓碑是一回事；树上挂着鲜血淋漓的头颅则是另一回事。当我的孩子们还小时，一个简单的去公园的路程变成了噩梦。现在，我的孩子们已经足够大，可以欣赏一个好笑话，我意识到我自己并不这样。为什么在这个世界上已经有真正的人遭受折磨时，我们还要把折磨变成娱乐？我没有要求禁止我不喜欢的装饰，但如果能限制我看到它们的时间会更好。

然后是竞争升级的问题。我的社区举办了盛大的万圣节庆祝活动，我不是开玩笑——我有一个邻居，每年都举办一个可以与专业鬼屋媲美的鬼屋。人们从城市各地开车来参观。虽然很有趣，但其他邻居可能会感到必须提高自己的万圣节游戏水平。艾琳告诉我，她甚至因为一个邻居在eBay上以高价买到一辆仙灰姑娘南瓜马车骷髅而失眠。这就是我们如何陷入骷髅军备竞赛的。

所有这些炒作都可能导致真正的万圣节疲劳，远在万圣节之前。当装饰已经出来两个月时，还有什么能在真正的万圣节前夜让孩子们惊喜和欢乐呢？

如果你非常喜欢万圣节，迫不及待地想展示出蒙在窗户上的木乃伊，有一种方法可以做到这一点，而不成为坏邻居。在做任何事情之前，请考虑以下几点：

**检查当地法规。**一些城市和住宅业主协会有具体的指导方针。了解你所在地区的规则，并遵守它们，否则可能会被罚款。

**考虑你的位置。**你住在郊区有大片空地吗？请尽情享受！你住在带有邮票大小庭院的联排别墅吗？保持简单。还要了解你的社区文化。有些地方以其夸张的季节性展示而闻名，甚至吸引游客。如果你住在那里，那就放开手脚加入。如果你不喜欢，那就接受你确实住在了这样的社区。

**考虑噪音和光亮。**除了万圣节精神，与住在15英尺之外的人一起生活，他有10个充气装饰品、五个有激光眼睛的骷髅和三只跳跃尖叫的猫，这确实是噪音和光亮过多——尤其是如果你让它们整夜亮着。体谅你的邻居，客观地看待你的装饰布置。

**考虑装饰的内容。**涉及大量血腥、恐怖或跳吓的装饰可能不适合你的地区。如果你喜欢这些，考虑把它们放在屋内，或者保留到万圣节当天，或者最多提前一周。另一个选项是适度调整。

**考虑儿童。**作为成年人，我（多少）可以选择自己看到什么和如何处理它。另一方面，年轻的孩子没有选择权，往往对可怕的万圣节装饰感到真正的恐惧。如果你住在有许多幼儿的社区，考虑保持装饰轻松愉快。

**即使你努力创造一个完全合适的季节性展示，仍然有人会找到不满的理由，你无法规划这些人。但你应该为那些有合理问题的人制定计划——比如灯光闪烁在他们的窗户里，或者幼儿出现新的噩梦。生活在社区的一部分是知道如何与那些与你共同生活的人礼貌地妥协。**

**在9月30日之后装饰房子不算无礼。**对于那些寻找装饰万圣节装饰的合适时间的可靠日期的人来说，我们给你这个：10月1日或之后。如果你早于这个时间装饰，可能有点无礼，尽管这肯定不是最严重的礼仪罪行，尤其是如果你的装饰氛围是轻松有趣的。但如果你展示的装饰是大多数人会觉得冒犯或令人不安的，或者你的装饰噪音和刺耳，以至于妨碍了邻居的日常生活，你一定会成为无礼的邻居。

**但除了邻居礼仪，万圣节可以成为人们真正团结在一起的伟大时刻，所以利用你的万圣节装饰来认识邻居，一起享受乐趣，并让每个人都安全快乐。**如果这涉及到仙灰姑娘骷髅南瓜马车，那就更好了。只是别让我黑夜时从旁经过。
articles.summary:
My friend Nic is so Halloween-obsessed that she has two entire rooms in her basement dedicated to storing her Halloween decor. While most people have guest rooms for human guests, hers host six (yes, six) of those 12-foot-tall giant Skellys. They’re also stuffed with more than 50 human-sized skeletons, a handful of dog and cat skeletons, flashing lights, noise machines and even a Christmas-sleigh tableau recreated with—you guessed it—skeleton reindeer.

So when she starts planning Oct. 31’s festivities in June, I just nod and hand her some candy corn. As for me, I’m on the opposite side of the spectrum: I’m a Halloween grinch. I really don’t decorate unless you count the orange flickering light bulbs I installed near my garage seven years ago and was too lazy to swap back out for real ones. But it goes beyond laziness. To be honest, I just don’t like Halloween. Little kids in costumes? Perfect, let’s do that every day. It’s everything else I could do without. Mostly, I hate the gory, terrifying yard displays because I am a giant scaredy-cat. There is a Ring camera video that still circulates among my neighbors of me getting so freaked out by one of those hands that pops out that I run away, screaming.

And yet Nic and I are the closest of friends! I think we balance each other’s holiday vibes. That said, there is one big point we disagree on: When is it OK to put out the Halloween decorations? Is it really rude to decorate your house early for Halloween? And how early is too early? The answer probably lies somewhere between her “right after the 4th of July” and my “the 4th of Never.” So for the purposes of this column, I’m defining “early” as anything before Oct. 1.

Now, put on your witch hat and let’s discuss.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more etiquette, holidays, humor, travel, tech and fun facts all week long.

The case for decorating early

Your house, your rules. This is honestly the best argument for decorating for any holiday whenever and however you like. You paid good money for that lawn, so you should be able to decorate it however you see fit (within the realm of public decency). And it seems like a lot of people are doing it. According to a 2024 YouGov poll, 52% of people reported seeing Halloween decorations out before October—and 13% before Labor Day. Yes, there are a solid number of folks setting up Skellys for back-to-school. (Some people even keep up their Skellys year-round!)

And it does make sense: If you love Halloween, the earlier you set up your decor, the more time you have to enjoy the fun. It also sparks a sense of neighborhood camaraderie by giving people some entertainment as they take their dog on its nightly poop walk. It may even inspire some of them to get a little more festive. In a world where HOAs dictate every paint color and bush placement, this is your chance to get a little bit wild.

Decorating early also helps you work around weather if you live in a place with a, shall we say, dramatic climate. When we lived in Minnesota, people hung their Christmas lights in September—not because they were incredibly jolly but because no one wants to be on a roof in December in a foot of snow and -10 degrees. Halloween decor also went up before the first storm, and yes, that meant sometimes you had both orange jack-o’-lanterns and red-and-green roof lights at the same time. Better than frostbite!

So is a giant skeleton torso crawling out of the lawn a bit extra for a Tuesday in September? Probably. But there’s a lot to be said about the specific type of joy and anticipation that nostalgia brings, and nothing triggers that feeling like decor. Who doesn’t have a wonderful fall memory of heading out with your friends, dressed as superheroes, running through the spookily lit neighborhood and gorging yourselves with candy? See? You’re smiling already.

The case against decorating early

“Your house, your rules” is true, but your house is (probably) located in a community of people, and those people get to have a say in their environment—including when that environment gets populated with the undead. And folks do have some feelings about this: A separate 2024 YouGov poll found that 39% of people said Oct. 1 through Oct. 15 was the earliest acceptable time to put up Halloween decor, and 24% said anytime after Labor Day was fair game. Only 4% said earlier than that was fine.

That line in the previous section about Halloween decor being “within the realm of public decency” is doing a lot of heavy lifting, and for me, this is where the debate really heats up. Funny skeletons and silly gravestones are one thing; bloody heads hanging from trees are another entirely. When my kids were little, a simple walk to the park became a waking nightmare. Now that my kids are old enough to appreciate a good scare, I’ve come to realize that I just don’t. Why do we turn torture into entertainment in a world that already tortures real people? I’m not asking to ban the decorations I don’t like, but it would be nice if we could limit the amount of time I have to spend seeing them.

Then there’s the issue of competitive escalation. My neighborhood goes all-out, and I do mean all-out—I have a neighbor who sets up a haunted house every year that rivals professional scare factories. People drive from all over the city to walk through it. And while it is fun, other neighbors may feel compelled to up their Halloween game too. Nic told me that she actually lost sleep when a neighbor managed to get a sold-out skeleton Cinderella pumpkin carriage on eBay. This is how we end up in a skeleton arms race.

All of this hype can lead to a very real Halloween fatigue, well before the big day. What’s left to surprise and delight trick-or-treaters on the real All Hallows’ Eve when it’s already been out for two months?

The etiquette of putting up your Halloween decorations early

If you simply adore Halloween and can’t wait to break out the mummy-trapped-in-your-window film, there is a way to do it without being the bad neighbor. Before you do anything, consider the following:

The rules

Some cities and HOAs have specific guidelines for exactly this. Find out the rules for where you live, and abide by them or risk paying a fine.

The type of neighborhood you live in

Are you in a rural area with tons of space around you? Go hog wild! Are you in a townhouse with a postage-stamp-sized yard? Keep it small. Also know your neighborhood culture. Some places are known for their devotion to over-the-top seasonal displays and may even attract visitors. If you live there, then feel free to join in with abandon. (And if you don’t like it, accept that that is just the type of neighborhood you moved into.)

How much you’re putting up

Halloween spirit aside, living 15 feet away from someone with 10 inflatables, five skeletons with laser eyes, and three cats that jump and scream is just a lot of noise and light—especially if you leave them on all night long. Be considerate of your neighbors, and take an unbiased look at your decor placement.

How gory or over-the-top it is

Displays that involve a lot of blood, gore and/or jump scares may not be appropriate for your area. If you love that stuff, consider putting it up inside your house or saving it for the big day or, if you must, the week of Halloween. Another option is to tone it down a little.

How many young children live nearby

I’m an adult and can choose (mostly) what I see and how to handle it. Young children, on the other hand, don’t get to choose and are often genuinely terrified of scary Halloween decorations. If you live in a neighborhood with a lot of very young kids, consider keeping the decor light and fun.

What you’ll do if someone is bothered by it

Even if you do your best to make a totally appropriate seasonal display, someone can still find a reason to be upset and you can’t plan around those folks. But you should have a plan for people with legitimate issues—like lights flashing in their windows or toddlers with new night terrors. Part of living in a community is knowing how to politely compromise with those who live in it with you.

The verdict

It is not rude to decorate your house for Halloween after Sept. 30. For people looking for a firm date of the acceptable time to put up Halloween decorations, we’re giving it to you: Oct. 1 or later. You may be a little rude if you put up your decorations earlier than that, although it certainly isn’t the most egregious etiquette crime, especially if your decor vibe is lighthearted fun. But you will definitely be the rude neighbor if you put up displays that most people would find offensive or disturbing, or if your decor is so loud and obnoxious that it impedes your neighbors from living their daily lives.

But beyond the actual neighbor etiquette, Halloween can be one of those great moments that really brings people together with their community, so use your Halloween decorations as a way to get to know your neighbors, have fun together and keep everyone safe and happy. And if that involves a Cinderella skeleton pumpkin carriage, even better. Just don’t ask me to walk past it after dark.

Why trust us

Reader’s Digest has published hundreds of etiquette stories that help readers navigate communication in a changing world. We regularly cover topics such as the best messages to send for any occasion, polite habits that aren’t as polite as they seem, email and texting etiquette, business etiquette, tipping etiquette, travel etiquette and more. We’re committed to producing high-quality content by writers with expertise and experience in their field in consultation with relevant, qualified experts. We rely on reputable primary sources, including government and professional organizations and academic institutions as well as our writers’ personal experiences where appropriate. We verify all facts and data, back them with credible sourcing and revisit them over time to ensure they remain accurate and up to date. Read more about our team, our contributors and our editorial policies.

  • YouGov: “When do you think is the earliest acceptable time to display Halloween decorations?”

articles.title: This Hidden iPhone Feature Can Save Your Life in a Car Crash—And Most People Don’t Even Know It Exists
articles.content:
几年前，我在俄克拉荷马州的州水质机构工作。我经常驾驶着一艘大船在乡间小路上行驶，或者悬挂在高速公路桥上采集水样——这些都在飞驰的巨型卡车（以及大量超速的汽车）卷起的尘土中进行。这工作让人紧张，但我从未发生过事故。而我的一位同事就没那么幸运了。

他一个人独自工作，就像我经常做的那样。他撞上了一只鹿，然后又撞上了树。幸运的是，他没有受伤，但他无法求助。于是他只能步行。走了几个小时。今天，他会掏出手机打电话求助——但如果他受伤无法动弹怎么办？如果你遇到车祸无法接触手机怎么办？事实证明，你的iPhone有一种即使你无法操作也能提供帮助的方式。

根据国家公路交通安全管理局（NHTSA）的数据，2024年（最新可用数据）发生了超过600万起非致命事故，以及超过160万起导致伤亡的事故。死亡人数接近4万。如果你被困在某条乡间小路上，独自一人，在黑夜里？情况可能会迅速恶化。

接下来，我将介绍一个非常实用的iPhone安全功能，它可以帮助你。这个功能使用方便，虽然不能预防车祸，但在你最需要的时候肯定能帮上忙。请继续阅读，了解这个重要的iPhone安全设置，你可能完全不知道它的存在。

iPhone有一个名为“碰撞检测”的功能。如果你驾驶或乘坐的汽车发生“严重”碰撞，包括前后相撞、侧面碰撞和翻车，你的iPhone将检测到车祸并通知紧急服务，即使你无法响应。

一旦你的iPhone或Apple Watch检测到严重车祸，这里是它如何工作的：

当碰撞检测感知到你发生了车祸后，你的iPhone会显示一个警报（“看起来你刚刚遇到了车祸”），并发出10秒的警报声。它还会大声读出警报，以便你无法触及手机时也能听到，并显示一个紧急呼叫滑块，这样你就能在有条件的情况下联系紧急服务。

如果你在10秒内没有启动滑块或取消警报，将开始一个30秒的倒计时。倒计时期间会伴随着苹果公司称之为的“响亮的呼啸声”和激烈的闪光灯。倒计时结束后，你的手机将拨打911报警。

在车祸后，你的iPhone和Apple Watch会显示相同的警报（“看起来你刚刚遇到了车祸”），你的手表会响铃并轻拍你的手腕10秒。Apple Watch会显示紧急呼叫滑块，你可以通过手表拨号并通话。

如果你在10秒内没有启动滑块或取消警报，将开始一个30秒的倒计时。倒计时期间会伴随着响亮的呼啸声和手机的激烈闪光，以及手表的轻拍。倒计时结束后，你的Apple Watch将拨打911报警。

即使你的手机不在车上，如果你的Apple Watch检测到严重碰撞，它也会显示警报（“看起来你刚刚遇到了车祸”）。它会响铃并轻拍你的手腕10秒，并显示紧急呼叫滑块。如果你的手表有蜂窝数据功能或连接了Wi-Fi，你可以通过手表拨号并通话。

如果你在10秒内没有启动滑块或取消警报，将开始一个30秒的倒计时。倒计时期间会伴随着响亮的呼啸声和激烈的手腕轻拍。倒计时结束后，如果你的手表有蜂窝数据功能或连接了Wi-Fi，它将拨打911报警。

所有搭载iOS 16或更高版本操作系统的iPhone 14及以上机型都具有碰撞检测技术。这项服务也是Apple Watch Series 8或更高版本、Apple Watch SE第二代或更高版本，以及Apple Watch Ultra或更高版本的标准功能，需要搭载watchOS 9或更高版本的操作系统。

碰撞检测功能默认开启，所以你无需启用它就能运行。不过，你应该仔细检查以确保你没有误关闭它。这个功能位于设置中的紧急求救选项中（见上方截图）。

你的设备还会通知你设置的紧急联系人。如果你在Apple健康应用中输入并启用了医疗ID信息（后面会有更多介绍），还会出现一个额外的滑块，这样一线救援人员可以在不需要你的密码的情况下访问这些信息。

对于安卓用户，谷歌Pixel手机（Pixel 4a及以上机型）有一个类似的功能，称为“车祸检测”，但需要手动开启。它默认是关闭的。

是的。如果你不希望你的Apple设备在车祸后联系紧急服务，你可以关闭这项服务（虽然我们强烈建议你保持其开启状态）。在设置>紧急求救中可以关闭iPhone上的功能。你的Apple Watch的碰撞检测设置也位于你的iPhone上，在Apple Watch>我的手表>紧急求救中。

如果你担心碰撞检测会干扰你的汽车的紧急响应功能，苹果表示它不会。你的汽车或你直接通过设备发出的紧急电话将如常接通（非紧急电话将被断开）。

如果你遇到了车祸但不需要帮助，你可以在它们联系紧急服务之前取消警报。如果你误拨了紧急电话，或者拨通后决定不再需要帮助，苹果建议你们保持通话并与EMS人员交谈以更新你的情况——不要挂断。

碰撞检测并不是唯一一个能帮助你保持安全的苹果安全功能。这里还有其他重要的设置，你应该了解并启用它们。

articles.summary:
Years ago, I worked for a state water quality agency. I’d drive around the back roads of Oklahoma hauling a big boat or dangle off a highway bridge collecting water samples—all while massive logging trucks (and plenty of speeding cars) zipped by in a cloud of dust. It was nerve-racking, but I never got in an accident. One of my co-workers wasn’t so lucky.

He was alone, like I often was. He hit a deer, then a tree. Luckily, he wasn’t injured, but he had no way to call for help. So he walked. For hours. Today, he’d whip out his phone and call someone—but what if he was injured and couldn’t? What if you got in a car wreck and couldn’t reach your phone? Well, it turns out your iPhone has a way to help even without your input.

According to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), there were more than 6 million nonfatal accidents in 2024, the most recent data available, and more than 1.6 million wrecks that resulted in injury. There were nearly 40,000 fatalities. If you’re stuck on some country road, alone, in the dark? Things could go south very quickly.

Below, I’ll take you through a really cool iPhone safety feature that can help. It’s easy to use, and while it won’t prevent car crashes, it can definitely help you when you need it most. Read on to learn about this important iPhone safety setting you probably had no idea existed.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more tech, cleaning, humor, travel and fun facts all week long.

What is the hidden iPhone feature that could save your life in a car crash?

It’s a feature called Crash Detection. If the car you are driving or traveling in gets in a “severe” crash, which includes front- and rear-end collisions as well as side-impact crashes and rollovers, your iPhone will detect the wreck and alert emergency services if you’re unable to respond.

Here’s how it works once your iPhone or Apple Watch detects a severe crash.

If you only have your iPhone

Once Crash Detection senses you’ve been in an accident, your iPhone displays an alert (“It looks like you’ve been in a crash”) and sounds an alarm for 10 seconds. It also reads the alert aloud to you, in case you cannot reach your phone, and displays an Emergency Call slider so you can contact emergency services if you’re able.

If you do not initiate the slider or dismiss the alert within 10 seconds, a 30-second countdown begins. The countdown is accompanied by what Apple calls “loud whoops” and aggressive flashing lights. After the 30-second countdown, your phone will dial 911 and report the crash.

If you have both your iPhone and Apple Watch

After a crash, your iPhone and Apple Watch display the same alert (“It looks like you’ve been in a crash”), and your watch chimes and taps your wrist for 10 seconds. The Apple Watch displays the Emergency Call slider, and you can call and speak through your watch.

If you do not initiate the slider or dismiss the alert within 10 seconds, a 30-second countdown begins. The countdown is accompanied by loud whoops and aggressive flashing on your phone, along with taps on your watch. After the 30-second countdown, your Apple Watch will dial 911 and report the crash.

If you only have your Apple Watch

Even if you do not have your phone in the car, your Apple Watch displays an alert (“It looks like you’ve been in a crash”) once it detects a severe collision. It also chimes and taps your wrist for 10 seconds and displays the Emergency Call slider. You can call and speak through your watch only if your watch has cellular data enabled or is connected to Wi-Fi.

If you do not initiate the slider or dismiss the alert within 10 seconds, a 30-second countdown begins. The countdown is accompanied by loud whoops and aggressive wrist-tapping. After the 30-second countdown, your Apple Watch will dial 911 and report the crash if your watch has cellular data enabled or is connected to Wi-Fi.

Do all iPhones have Crash Detection?

All models, starting with iPhone 14, that run iOS 16 or later operating systems have Crash Detection technology. The service is also standard on Apple Watch Series 8 or later, Apple Watch SE 2nd generation or later, and Apple Watch Ultra or later with watchOS 9 or later operating systems.

Crash Detection is on by default, so you do not have to enable it for it to work. That said, you should double-check to make sure you haven’t accidentally turned it off. This feature is located under Emergency SOS in Settings. (See the screenshot above.)

Your devices will also notify your emergency contacts if you have them set up. If you also have Medical ID information entered and enabled in the Apple Health app (more on this coming up), an additional slider will appear so that first responders can access that information without your passcode.

For Android users, Google Pixel phones (Pixel 4a and later) have a similar feature called Car Crash Detection, but it must be enabled. It is not on by default.

Can you turn it off?

Yes. If you do not want your Apple device to contact emergency services after a crash, you can turn off the service. (Though we highly recommend that you keep it activated.) Go to Settings > Emergency SOS to disable it on your iPhone. Your Apple Watch crash-detection settings are also located on your iPhone, under Apple Watch > My Watch > Emergency SOS.

If you’re worried that Crash Detection will interfere with your vehicle’s emergency response features, Apple says it will not. Emergency calls from your car or by you directly on your devices will be connected as usual (non-emergency calls will be disconnected).

What if you don’t actually need assistance?

If you have been in a crash but do not need assistance, you can dismiss the alerts before they connect you with emergency services. If you accidentally contact them, or connect and decide you no longer need help, Apple advises staying on the phone and speaking with the EMS personnel to update them on your situation—do not hang up.

Which other settings should you have activated in case of an emergency?

Crash detection isn’t the only Apple safety feature that can help you stay safe. Here are other important settings that you should know about and enable.

  • Medical ID: This feature holds important medical information that will be made available to emergency responders without a passcode in the event of a crash. Medical ID is found in the Apple Health app.
  • Emergency Contacts: This is also located in the Apple Health app, and adding your emergency contacts here will trigger an alert to them if you are involved in a crash. Make sure to have location services enabled in Emergency SOS (see below).
  • Emergency Calls & SOS: Found in your iPhone settings under Privacy & Security > Location Services, this feature will allow your phone to send your location to your emergency contacts. Note that messages cannot be sent if you do not use the Messages app as your default option.
  • Emergency SOS via Satellite: You don’t need to activate this one, but it’s an important feature to know about. On iPhone 14s or later, you have the option to use a satellite connection if your emergency call does not go through via normal means.
  • Emergency Bypass: This feature allows your chosen contacts to reach you even when your notifications are silenced. Open your contacts, tap each person, hit Edit > Ringtone, and toggle Emergency Bypass.

articles.title: Harry and Meghan’s California Home Will Cost *How* Much per Month—When They’re Not Even Living There?!
articles.content:
哈里和梅根夫妇将搬离美国返回英国，这对王室夫妇购置的加州豪宅面临巨额维护成本，尽管他们暂时离开，每年仍需支付数百万美元用于贷款、税费、保险和维护。

这对夫妇于2020年6月以1465万美元的价格购入位于加州蒙特西托的这座庄园，这座14500平方英尺的主屋拥有9间卧室和16间浴室。这座庄园曾在2015年以3400万美元的价格上市，当前估值仍高达数千万美元。蒙特西托是一处风景如画的社区，奥普拉·温弗里和罗布·洛均在此置业。

房屋拥有精心设计的花园、游泳池、网球场、冥想池和茶馆。内部配有专业厨房、多个壁炉、剧院、游戏室和葡萄酒藏室等豪华设施。这座庄园曾由俄罗斯亿万富豪谢尔盖·格里申所有，他同时拥有蒙特西托另一处名为“毒枭庄园”的豪宅。

尽管夫妇二人暂时离开，但每年仍需支付约65万美元的费用，其中包括：
- 贷款：夫妇二人在购房后申请了超过950万美元的贷款，按当前利率计算，每月需支付4万至4.3万美元，每年约50万美元。
- 税费：2023年税费约15万美元，且每年递增。
- 保险：蒙特西托被列为高火灾风险区，保险费用可能高达3万至4万美元。
- 维护：专家建议每年预留约30万美元用于日常和紧急维护，包括安全、花园养护等。

目前，夫妇二人计划将蒙特西托庄园作为美国住所，暂无出售或出租计划。尽管他们表示搬回英国是暂时的，但考虑到天价维护成本和英国法院对哈里等人起诉《每日邮报》和联合新闻集团案件的裁决，这一计划可能会有所变化。
articles.summary:
After six years in the States, Harry and Meghan are hitting the road and moving back to England. And they’re doing it soon. So what happens to that big pile of bricks they’ve been living in out in Montecito? The couple bought the place in 2020 after stints in Vancouver and Los Angeles, and from the pictures and clips we’ve seen, it’s something.

It’s also expensive. Montecito, California, is an unincorporated paradise tucked between the Santa Ynez Mountains and the Pacific Ocean along California’s Central Coast. Oprah Winfrey lives there. So does Rob Lowe. The views are stunning. And now that Harry and Meghan are leaving, their home will reportedly sit empty.

How much is that going to set them back? Will they need to sell? Take on renters? Ahead, I’ll break down the insane amount of money Harry and Meghan will have to spend just to keep the lights on in their Montecito mansion. Read on for the details.

Get Reader’s Digest’s Read Up newsletter for more royals, cleaning, humor, travel, tech and fun facts all week long.

How much did they buy the house for?

Harry and Meghan paid $14.65 million for the 7.5-acre estate in June 2020. The 14,500-square-foot main house, known as the Chateau at Riven Rock, has an ivy-covered entry and is flanked by elegant Italian cypress. It sits at the end of a long, curving driveway made from hand-cut local stone, the Los Angeles Times reported when the couple bought it.

The grounds have formal gardens, as well as a swimming pool, tennis court, meditation pond and teahouse. Inside, there’s a big chef’s kitchen (occasionally seen on Meghan’s Instagram), stone fireplaces, a theater, game room, wine cellar and just about anything else that you think can fit inside a home with nine bedrooms and 16 bathrooms.

Back in 2015, the same home was listed for more than double what Harry and Meghan paid: $34 million, according to the Times. Five years later, they bought the place from Sergey Grishin, a Russian billionaire who owned another Montecito property known as the Scarface mansion (it’s in the movie).

How much will it cost to maintain the property when they’re overseas?

A lot: Estimates are coming in at $650,000 and up per year—and that’s on the low end. Even though the house will reportedly sit empty, at least for now, there’s the mortgage, taxes, maintenance and other necessary expenses that come with home ownership.

Here’s how those costs break down.

Mortgage

The New York Post looked at property tax records and found that the couple took out a loan for more than $9.5 million soon after buying their home. The loan has an adjustable rate of 2.49% with a ceiling of 7.49% until 2030, when it resets.

According to their calculations, that gives the couple a mortgage payment of between $40,000 and $43,000 a month on a standard 30-year term. Multiply that by 12 months, and they’re looking at roughly $500,000 per year just to keep the bank happy.

Property taxes

Those same records show that Montecito is a pretty pricey enclave for taxes. Last year, the couple paid just shy of $150,000 in property taxes, a number that has been going up every year Harry and Meghan have lived there. Their first bill, in 2021, was $138,629.

Insurance

It’s hard to put a number on possible homeowners insurance for Harry and Meghan, but it’s high. Researchers at the University of California at Berkeley analyzed public data (2019–2023) and found that the median estimated single-family home insurance premium in the state was $182 for every $100,000 in home value. On a home costing $14.65 million, that’s about $26,660 per year—and that’s just the median.

The home is also in a high fire hazard severity zone, according to the Montecito Fire Protection District, so they definitely have wildfire coverage. A broker on Berkshire Hathaway’s website says rates for high-value estates in Montecito fire zones can easily reach $30,000 or $40,000 per year.

Home maintenance and groundskeeping

Real estate and financial experts advise earmarking 1% to 3% of your home’s value for yearly maintenance. The low end, 1%, is more typical for regular homeowners, but the rate goes up for luxury homes. Security, pool service, roof repairs, heating and cooling, maintaining the extensive grounds and gardens … the costs add up quickly.

Even at 2%, that’s nearly $300,000 that Harry and Meghan should set aside for ongoing and emergency maintenance. We’re not saying they’ll have to spend that every year, but it’s not nothing—and it could bring their yearly tally closer to $1 million.

Are they planning to move back or use this as a second house?

For now, the couple plans to use the Montecito home as their U.S. residence, and they have no plans to sell (or rent it out, for that matter).

Their kids, Archie and Lilibet, are enrolled in school in England this fall, so presumably the family will stay through the school year. But the couple currently says the move is “temporary,” according to TMZ, which also reports that Markle’s mom, Doria Ragland, is staying in California.

But with a British court ruling against Harry, Elizabeth Hurley, Elton John and others in their phone-tapping complaint against the Daily Mail and Associated Newspapers, and the enormous costs associated with maintaining the home, the situation could become more fluid as time goes on.

Will they be living on the royal dime in the U.K.?

No. When Harry and Meghan left Britain, they relinquished their royal duties and their royal paychecks. That will continue even though they are moving back into the palace’s sphere of influence. They will have to pay their own rent as well as security, which has been a point of contention for the couple for years.

The couple used to live in Frogmore Cottage on the Windsor grounds, but they gave up the lease at Charles’s request when Harry’s memoir, Spare, was released. Speculation is running wild as to where they’ll end up now, with London already ruled out, according to media reports.

Experts are currently betting on the English countryside, perhaps near Althorp, where Princess Diana grew up, or in the Cotswolds, where Harry and Meghan’s good friend Ellen DeGeneres lives.
